title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is computing 'Euler-Poincaré characteristics' with compact support of the moduli stacks M_{0,4}, \hat M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}, \hat M_{1,1}. He then refines them to classes in a suitable 'Grothendieck group' with rational coefficients, with the Tate class T(1) = [E^1] (the affine line) as generator.

(1) Compactified M_{0,4}. He writes \hat M_{0,4} = [P^1_λ / S_4], where the Klein group V ⊂ S_4 acts trivially. Its orbifold Euler characteristic splits into two parts:
- χ_!(U_{0,3}, S_4) = χ(P^1 − 3 points)/24 = −1/24 (computed on the previous page);
- the cusp orbit {0, 1, ∞}, a single S_4-orbit with stabilizer of order 8 (D_4), contributing 1/8.
Total: −1/24 + 1/8 = 1/12.

(2) The finer Grothendieck-group refinement. The convention is to stratify the coarse space by automorphism group and give each stratum the class [coarse stratum]/|Aut|.
- M^!_{0,4} = P^1 − {0, 1, ∞}, so its class is T(1) − 2.
- M_{0,4} has coarse space the j-line A^1. Over it there are three strata:
  - generic points, with automorphism group V of order 4: (1/4)(T(1) − 2);
  - j = 0 (λ = −j, −j²), with automorphism group A_4 of order 12: 1/12;
  - j = 1728 (λ = −1, 1/2, 2), with automorphism group D_4 of order 8: 1/8.
  Total: [M_{0,4}] = (1/4)(T − 2) + 1/12 + 1/8 = (1/4)(T − 1) − 1/24.
- \hat M_{0,4} adds one cusp with automorphism group of order 8: [\hat M_{0,4}] = (1/4)(T − 1) + 1/12.
- Under the 'augmentation' T(1) ↦ 1 (Euler characteristic, since χ_c(A^1) = 1) these three classes give −1, −1/24, 1/12.

Margin: these formulas hold over Z[1/6] and must be redone more finely over Spec Z. In characteristic 3 all the special λ-orbits collapse to λ = −1, with stabilizer all of S_4. In characteristic 2 the λ = −1, 1/2, 2 orbit runs into the cusps.

(3) \hat M_{1,1}. Its codimension-1 boundary is one cusp (the nodal cubic, automorphism group of order 2). Over Z[1/2] the Legendre form gives a morphism M_{1,1} → (M^!_{0,4}, S_3) (≅ M^!_{0,4}/S_3 since V acts trivially). This makes M_{1,1} a gerbe banded by {±1} over [U_{0,3}/S_3] in characteristic ≠ 2. Hence:
- [M_{1,1}] = ½[U_{0,3}, S_3] = 2[M_{0,4}] = ½(T − 1) − 1/12 (equation (79) on the next page);
- [\hat M_{1,1}] = ½(T − 1) + 5/12;
- the Euler characteristics are −1/12 and 5/12, the classical values.
The next page redoes M_{1,1} over Spec Z by stratifying the j-line E^1. It uses the sections j = 1728 and j = 0, meeting at the supersingular points in characteristics 2 and 3, where the automorphism groups have orders 24 and 12.
errors: Conceptual caveat: the 'groupe de Grothendieck convenable' is never defined. The assignment Σ [coarse stratum]/|Aut| is additive and specializes correctly to orbifold Euler characteristics. It does not specialize to F_q-point counts weighted by 1/|Aut|: that count gives #M_{1,1}(F_q) = q, while the formula gives (q−1)/2 − 1/12.

This convention also differs from the later Grothendieck ring of stacks (Ekedahl, Behrend–Dhillon), where for instance [B G] for a finite group G is generally not 1/|G|. So the refinement is valid only as a 'weighted coarse-space class', not as a genuine motivic class of the stack.
The gerbe statement (78) needs the base Z[1/2] for the Legendre form. The margin correctly flags that the Z[1/6] restriction matters for the strata.

ideas.what: Orbifold (rational) Euler characteristics of M_{0,4}, \hat M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}, \hat M_{1,1}, computed by stratifying by stabilizers (values −1/24, 1/12, −1/12, 5/12)
ideas.modern_name: orbifold Euler characteristic / χ of moduli stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for M_{1,1} (SL_2(Z), Serre's Euler characteristic of discrete groups); Harer–Zagier 1986 for general M_{g,n}

ideas.what: Lifting Euler characteristics of moduli stacks to classes in a Q-linear Grothendieck group generated by the Tate class T(1) = [A^1], with augmentation T(1) ↦ 1
ideas.modern_name: motivic classes of moduli stacks / Grothendieck ring of stacks (rational coefficients)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ekedahl (Grothendieck group of stacks, 2009); Behrend–Dhillon; point-count 'Serre characteristics' of M_{g,n} by Getzler and Bergström

ideas.what: M_{1,1} over Z[1/2] as a μ_2-gerbe over the S_3-quotient of the Legendre λ-line, giving [M_{1,1}] = 2[M_{0,4}]
ideas.modern_name: Legendre presentation of M_{1,1}; relation between M_{1,1} and M_{0,4}/S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Deligne–Rapoport, Mumford 'Picard groups of moduli problems')

ideas.what: Observation that the stratified count depends on residue characteristic (needs Z[1/6]); program to redo it over Spec Z with supersingular points of automorphism orders 24 and 12
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic/integral motivic classes of moduli stacks

missed.claim: An early attempt to give moduli stacks motivic classes in a Q-linear Grothendieck group refining orbifold Euler characteristics, uniformly over Spec Z[1/6] and then Spec Z. The convention chosen ([coarse stratum]/|Aut|) is the 'naive' one, not compatible with point counts. Historically noteworthy as a precursor to the Grothendieck ring of stacks, though not a missed result.
missed.quote: De façon plus fine, dans un "groupe de Grothendieck" convenable, on aura [M^!_{0,4}] = T(1) − 2 ... ces trois quantités ont d'augmentations égales resp^t : −1, −1/24, 1/12
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck anticipating motivic/stacky Euler-characteristic refinements (later Ekedahl, Behrend–Dhillon, Bergström–Getzler point counts). Also shows the ambiguity in choosing such a group, which later work resolved differently.

deep.surprise_reason: The numbers are classical. The mildly notable point is Grothendieck spontaneously refining stack Euler characteristics to Tate-motive classes with rational coefficients, and insisting on doing it over Spec Z with characteristic-2 and -3 strata. That anticipates later 'Grothendieck ring of stacks' work, but in an ad hoc convention that does not match point counts.
transcription_corrections: 'd'anneau[?] quotient 1' should read '(d'augmentation 1)'; 'ces trois quantités ont d'imagination[?] égales' should read 'ont d'augmentations égales resp^t'.
In the line with the crossed-out term, [M^!_{0,4}] = [M_{0,4}] is likely '[M^!_{0,4}] = [U_{0,3}] = T(1) − 2' (the second symbol is U_{0,3}, not M_{0,4}).
Margin reads roughly: 'valables au dessus de Z[1/6] — cf. 79 — peut-être disparaissent ... de faire le calcul plus fin au dessus de Spec Z ...'.
Last line: '[M_{1,1}] = ½[U_{0,3}, S_3] = 2[M_{0,4}]' (the 2 is the coefficient), followed by a crossed-out expression involving T(1).
